strengths: UniAP addresses a useful systems problem for large vision and language models: selecting pipeline boundaries together with DP, TP, and FSDP strategies under memory constraints. Automating these coupled choices could substantially reduce configuration effort.

Table 1 demonstrates meaningful practical gains. On ENVB-8, ViT-Huge reaches 45.58 samples/s versus Alpa’s 38.74, and Swin-Huge reaches 19.08 versus Galvatron’s 13.90. Llama-7B achieves the reported 3.80× improvement over Galvatron. Matching throughput while reducing planning time on several ENVA cases also has value.
Evaluation covers five model families and four hardware environments, including non-NVIDIA accelerators. Table 4 provides encouraging near-linear weak scaling from 16 to 64 DCUs.

The workflow, notation table, solver configuration, and hardware-aware BERT case study help explain the system. Appendix F reports a modest 3.59% average throughput-estimation error for the selected configurations, providing useful empirical support for the cost model.
weaknesses: The principal correctness concern is that the stated constraints do not enforce pipeline-stage order. For a two-layer edge u→v, assigning u to stage 2 and v to stage 1 satisfies the contiguity and placement constraints, but Equation (4) assigns zero cross-stage communication because it counts only j→j+1 edges. Thus the optimization can omit real transfers. Appendix B proves contiguity, which does not resolve this stage-order problem; nonadjacent cross-stage edges in general graphs are also unaccounted for.

The central MIQP formulation is incomplete as written. Equations (3) and (4) contain products of four decision variables when terms such as P_ui P_vi(S_u^T R_uv S_v) are expanded. These are not quadratic expressions. Auxiliary variables could reformulate them, but the manuscript does not provide that reduction or the resulting solver-ready constraints, preventing verification of what Gurobi actually optimizes.

The memory model does not establish the claimed protection against OOM. Algorithm 1 passes microbatch size b=B/c into CostModeling, and Section 3.2 scales activation memory by that input. However, GPipe without checkpointing retains activations across c forward microbatches. Equation (5) shows no corresponding accumulation term. The manuscript needs a schedule-consistent account of peak memory; Appendix F evaluates throughput estimation rather than memory feasibility.

The repeated claim of finding an optimal strategy exceeds the evidence. Appendix E specifies a 60-second limit and permits early termination with a gap below 4%, but achieved gaps and termination statuses are not reported. Moreover, optimality for an approximate cost model is distinct from optimal measured throughput. Section 3.5 bounds a time-capped search procedure, rather than establishing the stated complexity for globally solving the integer program.

The experiments do not isolate the proposed advantage over hierarchical optimization. Figure 6 compares combined parallelism against inter-layer-only and intra-layer-only variants, although the relevant baselines already combine both categories. A comparison using the same strategy choices, cost model, and execution backend is missing. The assertion that hierarchical optimization necessarily produces suboptimal solutions is also insufficiently justified; decomposition alone does not imply suboptimality.

The search-time improvements require qualification. UniAP’s reported time measures UOP and excludes preceding profiling, while Section 4.2 explicitly attributes part of the advantage to multithreaded Gurobi versus single-threaded baselines. These remain useful implementation results, but do not establish equivalent end-to-end or algorithmic speedups. Profiling and compilation breakdowns, thread budgets, the complete strategy dictionary, and repetition counts are insufficiently documented.

A secondary presentation inconsistency is that Figure 8 plots negative relative estimation errors although Equation (13) defines an absolute, nonnegative quantity. This should be corrected, but it is the formulation and validation concerns above that determine the Weak Reject recommendation.
